jobs.title: The tower district
jobs.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Architectural environment key art for Leg City Sounds, exterior city concept pass.
INPUT ROLES: Image 1 is the actual LCS live-scene screenshot and the strict camera / composition / primary building geometry reference. Images 2 and 3 are frames from the user's reference movie: visual mood, materials and architectural language ONLY. Do not copy the reference frames' composition, motion blur, fisheye, characters, or video capture artifacts.
Create one convincing photoreal architectural still, 16:9 widescreen. Re-render the first image as a real physical place, preserving camera, horizon, primary building footprints, relative heights, major tower silhouettes, recognizable central LCS building, and deep gaps. The visual target is the cold humid industrial city in the video. Overcast daytime after rain, no sun disc: soft grey-green ambient light, dirty ivory and aged warm-grey concrete, charcoal wet roofs, deep cool shadow, blue-grey atmospheric depth, a trace of dull olive paint. Restrained existing LCS magenta and rare tungsten amber are the only small active accents.
DENSITY: increase the functional layering of the existing rooftops significantly, denser than real Hong Kong. Accomplish it through medium-sized, legible objects and a more varied silhouette. Cluster mismatched HVAC banks, large bent-sheet ducts, pump housings, service sheds, braced old water tanks, steel access stairs, cable trays, restrained antenna forests, directional telecom panels and old microwave dishes. Keep every object structurally plausible, mounted, correctly scaled, with readable simple geometry. Add a few coherent sagging bundles crossing BETWEEN roof anchors. Have several major cable routes, not hundreds of arbitrary black scribbles. Place one or two plausible construction cranes in the middle distance, clear mast, jib and counterweight. Maintain some broad quiet roof patches and service access strips. Density comes from the count and arrangement of forms, not surface noise.
WINDOWS: retain disciplined repeated window grids and original architectural rhythm. Real dirty reflective dark glazing, broad coherent reflections of opposite buildings and pale sky, slightly uneven pane tints, localized grime near frames and under runoff. Through a minority of near windows show dim room depth, side reveals, broad curtains or blinds, a few pale interior ceilings. Glass must feel recessed behind the concrete frame rather than flat black holes. Most windows dark. No aquarium clarity, uniform opaque milkiness, mirror-chrome walls or rooms glowing everywhere.
HISTORY: selective rational maintenance patches, downward leak streaks at joints, broad faded paint, a few patched brick-infill areas, narrow oxidized metal edges. Include two or three old mounted advertisement boards with mostly torn-away paper, simple faded colour remnants, exposed board and obvious supports. One or two obsolete dead gas-neon sign frames with a few broken tubes, entirely unlit, no invented readable words. Nothing looks abandoned by an apocalypse: decades of occupation and repair, sparse evidence of current use.
IMAGE DISCIPLINE: crisp photographed large forms and clean edges, calm materials. Approximately 70 percent broad low-frequency surfaces, 25 percent medium-size equipment and architectural detail, 5 percent fine detail confined to the nearest cluster. Distant geometry progressively simplifies into haze. No random micro-greebles, fractal rust, gravel-like wall texture, gratuitous scratches everywhere, over-sharpening halos, film grain, painterly strokes, melted railings, tangled impossible piping, illegible new glyphs, or repeating equipment confetti. No people, plants, real brands, LEDs or giant new glowing advertisements. No contact sheet, captions, borders, UI or watermark.

SHOT A: Preserve the elevated broad district view, with the small LCS roof and slim block slightly right of center surrounded by lower roof terraces, the rounded old slab at left, the large framed industrial stack complex behind, and the nearest round-corner roof in the lower foreground. Give the foreground roof a readable trio of mechanical clusters; keep its water tank. Enrich the surrounding skyline with varied service structures and two distant idle cranes. The LCS tower remains a small inhabited anchor in a much larger city, not a new skyscraper. Keep the already existing magenta accents tiny. Foreground window bands should reflect neighboring vertical masses.
